html:
New York City is the largest city in the United States, on a great natural harbour at the mouth of the Hudson River. Since the early 1800s it has been the country's main port, its money centre and the door through which millions of immigrants arrived.

The land was the home of the Lenape. The Dutch founded New Amsterdam on Manhattan island in the 1620s as a fur-trading post. An English fleet took it without a fight in 1664, and it was renamed New York after the king's brother, the Duke of York. It was briefly the first capital of the United States, where George Washington took office in 1789.

Its rise came fast after that:

  • Brokers signed the agreement that began the New York Stock Exchange in 1792.
  • The Erie Canal of 1825 linked the harbour to the Great Lakes and made New York the leading port of the country.
  • Immigrants poured in from Ireland, Germany, Italy, eastern Europe and beyond; from 1892 most passed through Ellis Island.
  • In 1898 Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island joined into one city.

It drew exiles and inventors, among them the Cuban patriot José Martí and Nikola Tesla. Its skyscrapers rose in the 1920s and 1930s, and the Wall Street crash of 1929 began there. After World War II it became the home of the United Nations. On 11 September 2001 terrorists destroyed the World Trade Center, killing nearly 3,000 people.
